name: Cuts locked to the music

source.description: Measured in three inspected references: visual cuts fall on musical beats or audio hits far more often than chance.

technique: Scene cuts and word changes land on the soundtrack's beats or hits, so picture and sound feel like one gesture and the edit's rhythm is felt rather than noticed.
purpose: Rhythm and impact; makes fast cutting comfortable.
visual_behaviour: Each cut coincides with a drum hit or note onset; holds last whole numbers of beats.
mechanics: Beat grid from the track's tempo and phase; cue times snapped to the grid (or to detected onsets) within about one frame.

decomposition.timing: Measured: Measured at analyzer 1.2: ref-92c22222a2 60% of boundaries within 60 ms of the estimated 129 bpm grid (chance 26%), 80% within 50 ms of an onset (chance 41%); ref-392ee4d0f9 80% near an onset (chance 31%); ref-736d4ef2c2 40% near the 129 bpm grid (chance 26%, weak).

parameters.name: bpm
parameters.description: Track tempo (measure it; the corpus tool estimates it)

failure_modes: Snapping cuts that need reading time onto a fast grid
Using an estimated tempo without checking the phase by ear

implementation.approach: Studio.rhythm.grid(bpm, {offset}) and Studio.rhythm.snap for cue times; Studio.comp.wordBeats accepts a tempo grid. scripts/reference-corpus.py measures onset and beat alignment of a finished or reference cut.

additional_tooling.justification: Tempo and onset estimates come from the corpus tool's numpy analysis; Earshot or real-sfx on the render host can refine them.

limitations: Tempo estimates are autocorrelation-based and can lock to half or double tempo

provenance.observed: Cuts in the word section align with the estimated beat grid (measured 0.60 vs 0.26 chance).
Cuts coincide with audio onsets (measured 0.80 vs 0.31 chance).
Cuts sit near the estimated 129 bpm grid more often than chance, weakly (measured 0.4 vs 0.26).

evidence.notes: wordBeats times from a 120 bpm grid are exact.

licensing_notes: Technique only; measured from user-supplied references. No audio is reused.
